Date: 2027-06-05T09:12:00Z
Subject: Quick sync on dedicated capacity for launch (tokens/sec + SLO)

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the throughput looked great. We're finalizing internal runway for our beta launch and need a short write-up from Redwood on how to size Dedicated for our expected traffic pattern. High-level: 1) peak bursts of ~22k tokens/sec for ~45s every 10 minutes (inbound user prompts), 2) average sustained load ~2.5k tokens/sec, and 3) tail latency SLO 95th <= 300ms for generate endpoints.

Can you confirm: token/sec mapping to GPU slabs, recommended headroom for cold-cache bursts (we expect first-request KV misses), and whether a small reserved slab + shared pool makes sense for cost smoothing? If you can include assumptions (model variant, batch size, warm-up strategy) that would be perfect — procurement will need numbers for the commit.

I attached a synthetic traffic sample and our current rollout timeline.

Best,
Leah

Team — forwarding Helix's ask. Key asks: peak ~22k t/s bursts (~45s), sustained ~2.5k t/s, 95th <= 300ms. They flagged cold-cache concerns and want a recommended slab/commit + shared-pool mix.

Please run a short deal-specific model: assume the rtx-8x48-s variant (32-bit quantized), typical p99 kernel latencies we have, preferred batching of 8 with continuous-batching enabled, and KV-cache cold-hit penalty of ~70ms on first generation per shard. Output: tokens/sec per GPU, required GPUs for peak with 20% headroom, suggested reserved slab size (monthly tokens) + recommended burst policy (burst slab vs shared pool). Prioritize cost-efficiency but guarantee the latency SLO.

I've attached an initial RLS provisioning workbook (rls-provisioning-model-v1.xlsx) — please populate the 'Deal calc' tab.

Thanks,
Rafael

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-06T08:48:00Z
Subject: RE: FW: Quick sync on dedicated capacity for launch (tokens/sec + SLO)

Rafael / team — ran the numbers and summarized key assumptions first: model = rtx-8x48-s quantized (we use int8-path), per-GPU sustained generation throughput (steady-state, batching=8, 512-token avg request) = 3,200 tokens/sec; peak single-GPU burst with optimized kernel and prefetch = 6,400 tokens/sec for short windows (<=60s) if KV cache warmed; cold-cache first-gen penalty adds ~60-85ms to per-request latency and reduces effective t/s ~15% for that window.

Recommendations: 
- Reserved slab: 4 GPUs (rtx-8x48-s) to cover sustained load (4 * 3,200 = 12.8k t/s) — covers base plus room for predictable growth and telemetry spikes.
- Burst capacity: 3 additional GPUs in a shared burst pool (on a different allocation) to cover typical bursts. Combined peak capacity = (4+3)*6,400 effective peak-gpu-t/s = 44.8k t/s (warm). If we conservatively assume 15% degradation due to cold-cache on burst entry, expected peak delivered ~= 38k t/s — comfortably above 22k t/s requirement.
- Headroom: We recommend 20% safety on top of expected peak after cold-cache hit: reserve plan should guarantee ~(22k * 1.2) = 26.4k delivered t/s. Our combined warm capacity leaves ~11.6k t/s extra margin after conservative cold degradation, but only while KV contains warmed prefixes.
- Warm-up strategy: progressive canary pre-warm — route 5% of early beta traffic to static warmers (pinned requests) 10 minutes prior to main bursts; on each new shard, prefetch top-50 tokens of common prefixes. This reduces cold-hit penalty by ~40-60% in our tests.
- Cost trade: keeping 1 of the burst GPUs as a reserved hot standby reduces procurement risk for sudden peak growth (cost +6%), but lowers the chance of SLA fallback.

Actionable numbers (monthly commit guidance): 
- Suggested commit: 4 reserved GPUs (monthly) + 3 burst-capacity credits (preemptible-style or short-term reservations) for peak windows.
- Tokens budget: assuming 30 days, average sustained 2.5k t/s, expected monthly tokens = 2.5k * 3600 * 24 * 30 ~ 6.48B tokens. Recommend commit of 8B tokens to incorporate bursts and headroom.

I've updated the 'Deal calc' tab with per-GPU throughput, cold-hit factors, and cost estimates. See attached export and a short SLA proposal.

attachment: rls-provisioning-model-v1-dealcalc-export.csv (csv, 22KB)
attachment: sla-proposal-helix.pdf (pdf, 85KB)

Let me know if you want a more conservative sizing (extra dedicated slab) or a lower-cost alternative (more reliance on shared pool ramping with autoscaling).

—Priyom

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Leah Chen <leah@helix.ai>, ops@helix.ai
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-07T16:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick sync on dedicated capacity for launch (tokens/sec + SLO)

Hi Leah — thanks for the details and for the sample traffic. Priyom's team modeled a conservative and an optimistic plan; summary below and next steps.

Summary (short):
- Recommended commit: 4 reserved rtx-8x48-s GPUs for base + 3 shared burst GPUs.
- Expected delivered peak (conservative, accounting for cold-cache): ~38k t/s; this gives ~44% headroom on their 22k t/s requirement.
- Latency SLO (95th <= 300ms): achievable if warm-up can be done as recommended. With unmitigated cold-cache on first bursts, 95th could spike near the SLO — we strongly recommend the progressive pre-warm canary and pinned warmers approach.
- Monthly tokens commit recommendation: 8B tokens (covers sustained + bursts + 20% headroom).

Next steps:
1) Leah — confirm if procurement prefers a single-month pilot commit or a 12-month discounted slab. Our pricing team can surface both options; pilot gives flexibility but higher unit cost.
2) If pilot: we'll provision 3 burst GPUs as reserved hot-standby for the first 30 days to eliminate risk during onboarding (adds ~6% to monthly cost).
3) Ops: please share any additional high-frequency pattern (sub-minute spikes) so we can tune the batcher and warmers.

I'll drop the updated SLA and the HubSpot deal record with the suggested commit numbers (HLX-3492). DocuSign link for the pilot SOW will follow if you confirm pilot path.

Best,
Rafael

--
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
